today in the gospel of matthew jesus sums up the ten commandments into two great commandments for us.' the first you shall love the lord your god with all your heart, with all your soul and with all your mind, and the second is like it. you shall love your neighbour as yourself'. ' the commandments are a set of moral laws given to us by god to live good and just lives because he cares for us. jesus is telling us what kind of relationship we are to have with god and with our fellow human beings if we are to live happy and fulfilled lives and live in a just and fair community. we are to have a personal relationship with him putting him first in our lives, giving him his rightful place as our lord and creator who holds all things in being. with so many distractions in this world it is very easy for us not to put god first but if we do, all other things fall into place. we can have that relationship with jesus christ our redeemer who wants us to put our faith and hope in him because he loves so much and died on the cross to bring us eternal life. st. john's tells us god is love and all love comes from god; we are also called to love one another even our enemies, to forgive one another and to treat others as we would want to be treated. our christian faith enables us to walk on a journey with christ who purifies us and sanctifies us along the way enabling us to love him and our neighbour and so become transformed to his image and likeness and be ready to obtain eternal life with him. we must ask ourselves, “do i god and those around me as much as jesus loves me? this is the standard of love we must uphold. to love as jesus loved means to be willing to lay down our life for god and our neighbour.

. synodal evaluation assemble 2027: why are we holding an assembly? pope leo has asked every diocese to hold a pastoral assembly during the first half of 2027. each diocese is invited to review how it has progressed in becoming a more synodal church – a church in which all the baptised share responsibility for its life and mission. the diocese of kerry will hold its evaluation assembly on sat 10th april 2027. the assembly will review our experience since the publication of the synod’s final document in 2025. it will recognise where synodal ways of working are already developing, identify what may be hindering progress, and agree the next steps needed to strengthen the mission of the diocese. cahersiveen
